study_material.title: Reading Comprehension - Complete Study Notes
study_material.introduction: Reading comprehension gives a passage and asks questions on its content, tone, inference and vocabulary. The answer is always supported by the passage - never by outside knowledge. Speed comes from reading the questions first and scanning purposefully.
learning_objectives: Identify main idea versus supporting detail
Distinguish stated facts from valid inferences
Determine the author's tone and purpose
Manage time across passage and questions

concepts.heading: 1. Question Types
concepts.body: Factual (directly stated - locate and match), Inference (implied but not stated - must follow necessarily), Main idea (the passage's central point, not a single paragraph's), Tone/attitude (the author's stance), Vocabulary-in-context (meaning in THIS passage, which may not be the dictionary's first sense), and Structure (why the author included a paragraph).

concepts.heading: 2. The Efficient Method
concepts.body: Skim the questions first to know what to hunt for. Read the passage once at moderate speed, marking the topic sentence of each paragraph. Answer factual questions by returning to the text and pointing at the supporting line. Never answer from memory or from general knowledge.

concepts.heading: 3. Inference Discipline
concepts.body: A valid inference must follow necessarily from the text. If a statement is merely plausible or 'probably true in the real world', it is wrong. Reject options containing extreme words - always, never, all, none, only - unless the passage states them explicitly.

concepts.heading: 4. Tone Vocabulary
concepts.body: Common tone answers: objective/neutral (factual reporting), critical (finding fault), appreciative/laudatory (praising), sceptical (doubting), analytical (examining causes), optimistic, pessimistic, ironic, cautionary. Look at adjectives and adverbs the author chooses - they carry the tone.

concepts.heading: 5. Main Idea vs Detail
concepts.body: The main idea covers the WHOLE passage. A common wrong answer is true but too narrow (covers one paragraph) or too broad (covers more than the passage claims). Test each option: does it summarise everything, or only a part?

formulas: Every answer must be traceable to a line in the passage
Inference = necessarily true, not merely plausible
Reject extreme words unless explicitly stated
Main idea covers the whole passage, not one paragraph
shortcut_methods: Read the questions before the passage
Mark each paragraph's topic sentence as you read
For vocabulary questions, replace the word with each option and reread the sentence
common_mistakes: Answering from personal knowledge rather than the text
Choosing an option that is true but too narrow for a main-idea question
Spending too long on one difficult inference question
study_material.summary: Preview the questions, read once with purpose, and anchor every answer to a specific line - inference means necessary, not likely.
quick_revision_notes: Point to the supporting line for every answer

solved_examples.question: Passage: 'Remote work has reshaped corporate culture. Companies report higher productivity and lower attrition, yet many managers worry that spontaneous collaboration has weakened. Firms now experiment with hybrid schedules to capture both gains.' What is the main idea?
options: Remote work brings benefits but also concerns, prompting hybrid models
Managers dislike all forms of remote work
Productivity is the only measure that matters
solved_examples.correct_answer: Remote work brings benefits but also concerns, prompting hybrid models
solved_examples.step_by_step: The passage presents gains (productivity, attrition), a concern (collaboration), and the response (hybrid). Only the first option covers all three parts.
solved_examples.shortcut: The main idea must span every sentence, not just one.

solved_examples.question: Using the same passage, what is the author's tone?
solved_examples.step_by_step: The author presents both advantages and concerns without taking a side, and explains the resulting response - analysis, not advocacy.
solved_examples.shortcut: Presenting both sides evenly signals a neutral or analytical tone.

solved_examples.question: Using the same passage, which inference is valid?
options: Hybrid schedules attempt to preserve collaboration while retaining remote-work gains
Remote work will be abolished soon
Attrition is unaffected by work location
solved_examples.correct_answer: Hybrid schedules attempt to preserve collaboration while retaining remote-work gains
solved_examples.step_by_step: The passage says firms adopt hybrid to 'capture both gains' - directly supporting this inference. The others contradict the text or use extreme words ('all', 'abolished').
solved_examples.shortcut: Eliminate options containing all/never/soon unless stated.

solved_examples.question: Passage: 'The scheme was lauded for its ambition but faltered in execution, as funds reached only a fraction of intended beneficiaries.' In this context, 'faltered' most nearly means:
solved_examples.step_by_step: The contrast marker 'but' opposes 'lauded', and the following clause explains poor delivery - so 'faltered' means performed badly.
solved_examples.shortcut: Use the contrast word to fix the direction of meaning.

practice_questions.question: Passage: 'India's solar capacity grew from 10 GW in 2016 to over 70 GW in 2023, driven largely by falling panel prices and government auctions.' According to the passage, what drove the growth?
options: Falling panel prices and government auctions
practice_questions.correct_answer: Falling panel prices and government auctions
practice_questions.explanation: The passage names exactly these two drivers.

practice_questions.question: Using the same passage, solar capacity in 2016 was:

Passage: 'Sleep is not passive rest. During deep sleep the brain clears metabolic waste, consolidates memory and regulates hormones. Chronic sleep loss therefore affects far more than alertness.' The main idea is:
options: Sleep performs essential biological functions beyond rest
Sleep is only about feeling rested
Hormones are the most important part of sleep
People should sleep exactly eight hours
practice_questions.correct_answer: Sleep performs essential biological functions beyond rest
practice_questions.explanation: This covers the whole passage; the others are too narrow or unsupported.

practice_questions.question: Using the sleep passage, which inference is valid?
options: Sleep has no effect on hormones
Everyone needs the same amount of sleep
practice_questions.explanation: Since deep sleep consolidates memory, losing it may impair memory - a necessary inference.

practice_questions.question: Passage: 'The report's conclusions rest on a sample of just forty respondents, yet its authors generalise confidently to an entire industry.' The author's tone is:
practice_questions.explanation: 'Just forty' and 'yet ... confidently' signal disapproval of the methodology.

practice_questions.question: Passage: 'Her prudent management of the budget left the department with a surplus in a difficult year.' In context, 'prudent' means:
practice_questions.explanation: Producing a surplus in a hard year indicates careful, sensible management.

practice_questions.question: Passage: 'Electric vehicle adoption depends less on battery technology today than on charging infrastructure. Where chargers are dense, sales climb sharply; where they are sparse, even generous subsidies have limited effect.' Which inference is valid?
options: Subsidies alone may not raise EV sales without adequate charging access
Battery technology no longer matters at all
Charging infrastructure is cheap to build
practice_questions.correct_answer: Subsidies alone may not raise EV sales without adequate charging access
practice_questions.explanation: The final clause states subsidies have limited effect where chargers are sparse. The others are extreme or unsupported.

practice_questions.question: Using the EV passage, the author's main purpose is to:
options: Explain what most influences EV adoption
practice_questions.correct_answer: Explain what most influences EV adoption
practice_questions.explanation: The passage compares two factors and identifies infrastructure as decisive - explanation, not advocacy.

topic_test.title: Reading Comprehension - Topic Test
instructions: +1 for correct, -0.25 for wrong, 0 for unattempted.
Each question carries its own short passage. Answer only from the passage.

questions.question: Passage: 'The library will remain closed on Mondays for maintenance. Members may still return books through the drop box outside the main entrance.' What can members do on Mondays?
options: Return books via the drop box
questions.correct_answer: Return books via the drop box
questions.explanation: Explicitly permitted in the second sentence.

questions.question: Passage: 'Bamboo grows faster than almost any other plant, with some species adding a metre a day. This rapid growth makes it a promising renewable material.' Why is bamboo promising?
options: Because its rapid growth makes it renewable
Because it is stronger than steel
Because it is inexpensive to transport
Because it grows only in Asia
questions.correct_answer: Because its rapid growth makes it renewable
questions.explanation: The passage links growth speed directly to its promise as a renewable material.

questions.question: Passage: 'Many start-ups fail not because their product is poor but because they scale before finding genuine demand. Growth spending then outruns revenue.' The main idea is:
options: Premature scaling, not product quality, often causes start-up failure
questions.correct_answer: Premature scaling, not product quality, often causes start-up failure
questions.explanation: This captures the contrast the passage draws.

questions.question: Using the start-up passage, which inference is valid?
options: Confirming demand before scaling may reduce failure risk
Start-ups should never spend on growth
questions.correct_answer: Confirming demand before scaling may reduce failure risk
questions.explanation: Follows logically from the stated cause of failure.

questions.question: Passage: 'The committee's response was tepid at best; members offered polite nods but committed to nothing.' In context, 'tepid' means:
questions.explanation: 'Polite nods but committed to nothing' defines lukewarm enthusiasm.

questions.question: Passage: 'Urban trees lower street temperatures by several degrees, reduce runoff during heavy rain, and improve air quality. Yet city budgets rarely fund their maintenance.' The author's tone in the last sentence is:
questions.explanation: 'Yet ... rarely fund' signals disapproval of the funding gap.

questions.question: Passage: 'Automation has eliminated many routine clerical roles, but demand for workers who can interpret and act on automated output has risen. The net effect on employment is therefore contested.' Which statement is best supported?
options: Automation both removes and creates categories of work
Automation has clearly reduced total employment
Automation has no effect on jobs
All clerical workers are now unemployed
questions.correct_answer: Automation both removes and creates categories of work
questions.explanation: The passage names both an elimination and a rise in demand, and calls the net effect contested.

questions.question: Using the automation passage, the phrase 'the net effect is contested' implies:
options: Experts disagree about the overall impact
The effect has been precisely measured
There is no effect at all
questions.correct_answer: Experts disagree about the overall impact
